name: Scintillating Bubble Chamber (SBC)
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).
No official SBC website was found; the Institute of Particle Physics (Canada) project page lists SNOLAB as the laboratory. The website link is therefore empty.

The 30-g xenon bubble chamber (operated at Northwestern University in 2016 and later) is a precursor device, not an SBC detector at either laboratory; its two papers are recorded as technology-milestone results. A CEvNS version at a reactor site is a stated future option, not a proposal with a named host, so it has no record.
SNOLAB's 26 May 2026 laboratory layout slide lists SBC under 'Ladder Labs'; whether that marks a current or a future allocation is not stated, so no hall is asserted.

physics_goals.quote: The Scintillating Bubble Chamber (SBC) Collaboration is developing liquid-noble bubble chambers for the quasi-background-free detection of low-mass (GeV-scale) dark matter and coherent scattering of low-energy (MeV-scale) neutrinos (CE$\nu$NS).
physics_goals.value: Quasi-background-free detection of low-mass (GeV-scale) dark matter and coherent scattering of MeV-scale neutrinos (CEvNS)

summary.plain: SBC builds bubble chambers filled with superheated liquid argon that give both bubbles and light when something hits them. A 10-kg test chamber operates in a Fermilab tunnel; an identical, cleaner copy for a low-mass dark matter search is being built at SNOLAB.
summary.technical: Scintillating bubble chambers: 10-kg liquid-argon (doped ~10-100 ppm Xe) bubble chambers with cameras, SiPMs and piezo sensors, aiming at ~100 eV nuclear-recoil thresholds for 1-10 GeV/c^2 WIMPs and reactor CEvNS. SBC-LAr10 (Fermilab, MINOS tunnel) calibrates the response; a functionally identical SBC-SNOLAB chamber is under construction for the first dark-matter search (projected spin-independent sensitivity ~1e-43 cm^2 at 1 GeV/c^2). Technology demonstrated with a 30-g xenon bubble chamber at Northwestern (2016-17) and extended to 0.50 keV (2025). No dark-matter or CEvNS physics result was found in the sources read.
